刘祥 ( Phonetic pronunciation: shee-AHNG lee-OH )

Welcome!
I’m a PhD candidate in Economics at the University of Minnesota. I will be on the job market in 2027-28.
My research interests lie at the intersection of IO, international trade, and growth and development. My current work focuses on how transportation markets and global shipping networks shape trade costs, market access, and industrialization and development in emerging economies, using both empirical and theoretical tools.


Thomas Holmes (Chair), Erzo Luttmer (Co-Chair), and…

title: Teaching
text:
Instructor, ECON 4431W: International Trade Undergraduate; Fall 2025 & Spring 2026 Recognition. Distinguished Instructor, Fall 2025.



Course. ECON 4431W: International Trade.


Role. Instructor.


Description. This course studies the causes and consequences of international trade, with emphasis on the economic mechanisms behind trade patterns, trade policy, distributional effects, and globalization. Students learn to use economic models and empirical evidence to evaluate trade-related questions.


Enrollment. 57 students in Fall 2025 and 54 students in Spring 2026.


Materials. Syllabus is here, and selected teaching materials are available upon request.





Teaching Assistant, ECON 1101: Principles of Microeconomics Undergraduate; Fall 2023 & Spring 2024 Recognition. Distinguished TA, Fall 2023 & Spring 2024.



Course. ECON 1101: Principles of Microeconomics.


Role. Teaching Assistant.


Description. This course introduces core concepts in microeconomics, including consumer choice, producer behavior, markets, welfare, externalities, market power, and the role of public policy.


Enrollment. 240 students.


Materials. Discussion materials and teaching notes are available upon request.
